_about: Published, founder-approved data for the Borrowed Garden Provider Explorer. Generated by atlas-tools/build-borrowed-garden-provider-universe.py from the Atlas read-back and the approved wording. Do not hand-edit.

tabs.label: Garden-sharing services
tabs.note: Services that introduce garden owners to people who want to grow.

orgs.name: Community Roots
orgs.subtitle: Soil Mates garden-share programme
orgs.relationship: PlotNua has no relationship with Community Roots.
orgs.offers: A garden-share programme, Soil Mates, that pairs people who have a garden with people nearby who want to grow food. Each pairing receives a raised bed, compost, seeds and an online growing course.
orgs.where: Dublin, where it has made pairings since 2022, with a programme in the Liberties, Dublin 8. Six local projects have been started through ChangeX, including Rush, Co. Dublin.
orgs.how: A local volunteer coordinator matches garden owners with growers and introduces them at a pairing meeting.
orgs.evidence: ChangeX and The Wheel (Community Roots job notice), checked 13 October 2026; ChangeX (Rush project), checked 16 September 2026

orgs.name: Homegrown.ie
orgs.subtitle: Online matching service, free to join
orgs.relationship: Early and unproven. PlotNua has no relationship with Homegrown.ie.
orgs.offers: A free online service where people looking for growing space and people with spare garden or land register separately.
orgs.where: Starting in Irish cities, suburbs and nearby towns.
orgs.how: Exact addresses stay private and contact details are shared only when both people say yes; any arrangement is then made directly between them. On its own published figures it has 78 grower requests, 3 offers of space and no matches so far, and the insurance it hopes to arrange is not yet in place.

tabs.label: Other growing opportunities
tabs.note: Council-run allotments. These are not garden-sharing services: they are council plots with their own waiting lists.

orgs.name: Dublin City Council
orgs.subtitle: Allotments and community gardens
orgs.relationship: PlotNua has no relationship with Dublin City Council.
orgs.offers: Council-run allotments and community gardens at nine sites. This is not garden-sharing.
orgs.where: Dublin city. Most of the listed sites are in Dublin 8 and Dublin 12.
orgs.how: You email the site you want and join its waiting list; licences are assigned as plots become free. The council says all available allotments are currently assigned.

orgs.name: Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council
orgs.subtitle: Allotments
orgs.relationship: PlotNua has no relationship with Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council.
orgs.offers: Council allotments at two sites: Goatstown (136 plots) and Shankill (95 plots). This is not garden-sharing.
orgs.where: Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown. Residents only, one plot per person.
orgs.how: Plots are allocated first come, first served from a waiting list. The council is not currently accepting applications because both waiting lists are extensive (its notice is dated September 2024).

orgs.name: Fingal County Council
orgs.subtitle: Allotments
orgs.relationship: PlotNua has no relationship with Fingal County Council.
orgs.offers: About 900 council allotments across four sites: Balbriggan, Skerries, Turvey and Powerstown. This is not garden-sharing.
orgs.where: Fingal. Only Fingal residents can apply, with one plot per household.
orgs.how: Applications open once a year, in January, and each site's waiting list is capped at 50. For 2026 Powerstown and Turvey took no new applications because their lists were full.
orgs.evidence: Fingal's 2026 application form and fingal.ie, checked 13 October 2026
